title: Ledger fragments had no compaction, no helpers to write them, and eight probes still parsed the raw backlog file, so a fragment-closed row read as open to them

source.ref: the follow-ups HYG-145 (ADR-1635) deferred by orchestrator ruling, 2026-09-29

detail: FILED AND CLOSED 2026-09-29, the deferred half of HYG-145 (ADR-1635 decision 8). WHAT CLOSED IT. (1) Compaction: compactLedger() in scripts/lib/ledger.mjs and `pnpm ledger:compact [--check]` fold every fragment into docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json and docs/DECISIONS.md and delete them; the new base files are the merged view serialised as the base always was, so the view is identical before and after and a second run changes nothing; a broken fragment refuses the whole compaction. Run by a housekeeping PR past 30 fragments (owner ruling), which check:backlog now names. (2) Helpers: `pnpm ledger:close <ID> --verify-file <path> --note <text>` (probe read from a file, so no shell quoting; a .json file is a whole verify object), `ledger:add <row.json> --wave W7`, `ledger:adr <adr.md>`, `ledger:next [PREFIX]`. They fold into a fragment the branch already holds (foldEdit), so a row keeps one file. (3) Probes: PROG-D7, PROG-R10, LIVE-034, HYG-108, LIVE-176, HYG-023, LIVE-447 and LIVE-478 read the merged view, written as patch fragments. (4) The orchestrator scratchpad extractor (extract-ledger.mjs, which feeds build-ledger) reads through the loader when LEDGER_ROOT names a checkout; it is not in the repo. Tests: compaction round-trip, byte stability, broken-fragment refusal, closeEdit/foldEdit/nextFree.

verify.note: Measures the consequences in a fixture through the real CLI: ledger:close writes a fragment that closes the row in the merged view; ledger:compact leaves zero fragments with the merged view byte-identical before and after, and a second compaction does not change the base files. Then this tree: none of the thirteen probes that read row status or the slate parse the raw backlog file. Fails on main (no compactLedger), and the raw-read check names all eight on main.
